conventions.convention: The coefficient ring is R = Z[A±1], with A indeterminate and δ = −A²−A⁻². Generators are finite framed unoriented links represented by embedded annuli in the manifold interior; the empty link is allowed.

In an orientation-preserving crossing chart, the overstrand runs southwest to northeast. The A-smoothing pairs left endpoints and right endpoints with coefficient A; the B-smoothing pairs top endpoints and bottom endpoints with coefficient A⁻¹. Smoothed strips have blackboard framing.
A positive full twist is the curl whose A-smoothing is a straight strip plus a trivial circle; a negative twist has that B-smoothing. Their scalar factors are −A³ and −A⁻³, respectively.

Framing corrections are integers relative to the blackboard framing, positive for A-type twists. An A-type Reidemeister I insertion decreases the correction by one; a B-type insertion increases it by one. Diagram existence and equivalence assume countable choice.
The S³ evaluation sends the empty link to 1 and a zero-framed trivial circle to δ; for nonempty diagrams it is δ times the normalized nonempty bracket, multiplied by the framing correction.
Annular states assign δ to each disk-bounding circle and z to each essential circle. The empty state contributes 1. Full AC is assumed for the annular classification branch.

Collar products use the orientation pulled back from the ambient manifold. Their action glues only closed framed links into an outer subcollar; naturality requires productwise compatibility of the specified collars.

load_bearing.statement: For a smooth oriented 3-manifold M, the Kauffman bracket skein module is the free Z[A±1]-module on framed unoriented link isotopy classes, including the empty link, modulo [L×] − A[LA] − A⁻¹[LB] and [L ⊔ O] − δ[L], where δ = −A²−A⁻² and O is a zero-framed trivial circle in a ball disjoint from L.

Assuming countable choice, every framed link in the interior of a planar-annulus product admits a regular annular diagram with integer framing corrections. Framed-isotopic links have diagrams related by finitely many annular planar isotopies and local Reidemeister moves, with the stated framing-correction rule. The corresponding planar assertion holds for framed links in S³.

Assuming countable choice, E(∅) = 1 and, for nonempty L with diagram D and total framing correction m, E(L) = δ(−A³)^m ΣS A^(a(S)−b(S))δ^(|S|−1) is independent of diagram and correction and induces an R-linear map from the S³ skein module to R.

Assuming AC, Ψ(D,m) = (−A³)^m ΣS A^(a(S)−b(S))δ^u(S)z^e(S) is independent of the regular annular diagram and framing correction and induces an R-linear map from the solid-torus skein module to R[z], with Ψ(∅) = 1.
For a framed link with a specified component in a smooth oriented 3-manifold, the positive and negative twists defined in the Statement satisfy [L⁺] = −A³[L] and [L⁻] = −A⁻³[L].
Assuming countable choice, the Kauffman bracket skein module of S³ over R = Z[A±1] is freely generated by the empty link. A zero-framed trivial circle represents δ[∅].

Assuming AC, the classes [z^n], n ≥ 0, of parallel blackboard-framed annular core curves, with z⁰ the empty link, form an R-basis of the solid-torus skein module. The R-linear map J:R[z] → K_A(𝒜 × [−1,1]) sending z^n to [z^n] is an isomorphism.

Orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms induce functorial R-module isomorphisms of skein modules. A specified oriented surface product collar gives a width-independent unital associative left action by closed-link collar gluing, natural under diffeomorphisms respecting those collars.
